answers.how: The astronaut is approximately 39 px tall, giving 2.2/39 m/px. A smooth fit to its tracked position gives a speed of about 29.9 px/s at 0.5 s.
Differentiating the fitted pixel trajectory gives an acceleration magnitude of about 44.5 px/s² at 0.5 s; multiply by 2.2/39 m/px.
The fitted position trajectory gives about 47.2 px/s at 1 s. Convert using the astronaut's 39 px height corresponding to 2.2 m.
The fitted trajectory gives an acceleration magnitude of about 24.7 px/s² at 1 s, converted using 2.2/39 m/px.
The fitted position trajectory gives about 52.1 px/s at 2 s; multiply by the height-derived scale of 2.2/39 m/px.
The fitted trajectory gives an acceleration magnitude of about 14.8 px/s² at 2 s; multiply by 2.2/39 m/px.
The fitted position trajectory gives about 17.5 px/s at 3 s, converted using the astronaut's 2.2 m height over approximately 39 px.
The fitted trajectory gives an acceleration magnitude of about 54.3 px/s² at 3 s; multiply by 2.2/39 m/px.
